content.user_title: Build Azure Queue Workflows in TypeScript
content.value_statement: Azure Queue Storage code often needs precise SDK patterns for authentication, message visibility, and retries. This skill provides focused JavaScript and TypeScript examples for queue clients, messages, encoding, and SAS generation.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation guidance for the official Azure Queue Storage SDK packages.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential, connection string, shared key, and SAS token client setup.
Covers queue creation, listing, deletion, properties, and metadata operations.
Explains send, receive, peek, update, delete, and clear message operations.
Provides worker, poison message, and visibility extension patterns.
Includes message encoding, SAS generation, error handling, type references, and service limits.
limitations: Does not execute SDK calls or provision Azure resources by itself.
Does not include a runnable project, tests, or CI configuration.
Requires valid Azure credentials and storage account setup outside the skill.
Examples may need adaptation for browser, Node.js, and SDK version differences.

use_cases.title: Implement Queue Producers
use_cases.description: Create TypeScript services that send structured messages with visibility and time-to-live options.

use_cases.title: Build Worker Consumers
use_cases.description: Receive batches, process messages, delete successful work, and route repeated failures to a poison queue.

use_cases.title: Review Queue Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare authentication methods, SAS generation, platform limits, and message encoding choices.

prompt_templates.title: Connect to a Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to connect to Azure Queue Storage in TypeScript using DefaultAzureCredential. Explain the required environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Send and Receive Messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Azure Queue Storage message sending and receiving to a TypeScript service. Include visibility timeout and delete-after-success behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Worker
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a queue worker for Azure Queue Storage that handles batch receive, retries, poison messages, and long-running visibility extension.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Queue Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Queue Storage TypeScript implementation for authentication choices, duplicate processing risks, encoding issues, and SAS token exposure.

output_examples.input: I need a worker that processes Azure Queue messages safely.
output_examples.output: A processing plan covering batch receive settings, visibility timeout, success deletion, retry behavior, and poison queue routing.

output_examples.input: I am unsure which Azure Queue authentication method to use.
output_examples.output: A comparison of DefaultAzureCredential, connection strings, shared keys, and SAS tokens with Node.js and browser boundaries.

output_examples.input: My queue messages fail during long processing jobs.
output_examples.output: Guidance for extending visibility timeouts, updating pop receipts, and avoiding duplicate processing during long tasks.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential when the runtime supports managed identity or Microsoft Entra authentication.
Delete messages only after successful processing, and use dequeue counts for poison handling.
Set visibility timeout and message time-to-live values based on real processing duration.
anti_patterns: Do not store storage account keys or SAS tokens directly in source files.
Do not process messages without a retry and poison queue strategy.
Do not assume peeked messages can be deleted because they do not include pop receipts.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure commands for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides SDK guidance and examples. You must run code in your own Azure environment.

faq.question: Which SDK package does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers @azure/storage-queue for JavaScript and TypeScript, with @azure/identity for recommended authentication.

faq.question: Can it help with poison messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to use dequeue counts and move repeated failures to a separate poison queue.

faq.question: Does it support browser usage?
faq.answer: Partly. Anonymous and SAS access can work in browsers, but shared key credentials and SAS generation are Node.js only.

faq.question: Does it explain message encoding?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers default Base64 behavior and custom text or encoder settings.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It can guide production code, but you still need project-specific testing, monitoring, and credential management.
